LegalPages.legalIntro: 41BIT LLC is the sole operator of the hosted Epora web application and API and the sole contracting party for this service. Epora Wallet is a product name, not a separate legal entity. Individual developers and contributors are not parties to your service agreement and give no personal guarantees by contributing to the software. Send service claims, legal notices, and privacy requests to 41BIT LLC using the details below. This does not remove rights or liabilities that applicable law does not allow these terms to exclude.
LegalPages.termsIntro: These terms form an agreement solely between you and 41BIT LLC for the hosted Epora web application and API. Read them before accepting the beta notice. If you do not agree, do not connect a wallet or use the transaction features.
LegalPages.termsBetaBody: Epora is experimental beta software. No security audit of the application or smart contracts has been completed. Internal reviews and tests are not an independent security audit. The software may contain serious errors or vulnerabilities.
LegalPages.termsLossBody: You accept the risks of using the beta, including permanent loss, theft, or locking of all funds and other assets you use with it. Bugs, attacks, lost keys, malicious participants, incorrect permissions, failed recovery rules, or unavailable services can cause loss. Only use funds you can afford to lose. No recovery outcome is guaranteed.
LegalPages.termsControlBody: You authorize transactions through your connected wallet. Epora does not receive your seed phrase or private keys. You must check the network, addresses, amounts, fees, permissions, and transaction details before signing. Blockchain transactions may be irreversible. 41BIT LLC cannot promise to reverse a transaction, unlock funds, or recover lost keys. Network fees may apply even when an intended operation fails.
LegalPages.termsResponsibilitiesBody: Use the service only if you can legally enter this agreement. You must have authority over the wallets and assets you use. Keep keys and recovery material secure. Confirm that co-signers, spenders, payees, and beneficiaries are correct and understand their roles. Follow applicable laws and meet your own tax obligations. Do not attack the service, bypass access controls, misuse personal data, or disrupt other users.
LegalPages.termsServiceBody: The beta may change, be interrupted, or end. Providers and wallet software can fail or change their services. The web application does not guarantee continuous access to blockchain data or transaction submission. A website update does not necessarily update existing on-chain contracts. Check the terms and risks again when a new version requires acceptance.
LegalPages.termsAdviceTitle: No advice or protection against loss
LegalPages.termsAdviceBody: The application supplies software tools, not financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Displayed balances, projections, and transaction previews can be wrong or incomplete. These terms do not promise insurance, compensation, or protection against losses. A beta acknowledgement is not a deposit guarantee.
LegalPages.termsWarrantyBody: To the extent applicable law allows, the software is provided as is and as available, without warranties of correctness, security, availability, or fitness for a purpose. To that same extent, the Released Parties exclude liability for losses arising from use or inability to use the beta, including loss of funds, assets, data, or profits. These exclusions do not apply to fraud, gross negligence, or intentional misconduct, or where applicable law prohibits them. Nothing in these terms removes mandatory consumer rights or other rights that cannot lawfully be waived.
LegalPages.termsPrivacyBody: The privacy policy explains how the service handles data. Accepting these terms is not blanket consent to optional data processing. Wallets, blockchain networks, chain-data providers, and other services may have their own terms and privacy policies. Epora's original source code remains subject to the MIT License.
LegalPages.termsContactBody: Contact 41BIT LLC at the address below about these terms or a problem with the service. Applicable law determines your rights and the courts available to you. These terms do not impose mandatory arbitration or waive access to a court where that right applies.
LegalPages.privacyIntro: 41BIT LLC is the controller responsible for personal data it processes to operate the hosted Epora web application and API. Send privacy requests to 41BIT LLC, the sole service operator, using the contact below. This policy does not govern independently operated wallets, public blockchain participants, or copies of the software hosted by others.
LegalPages.privacyDataBody: The service processes wallet addresses, public key hashes, public transactions, balances, contract configuration, and participant roles. Its indexer collects public blockchain records, including participants named by other users who may never visit Epora. Proposal functions store titles and descriptions, transaction data, creator key hashes, collected signatures, and timestamps. Wallet sign-in stores a public key hash and first and latest sign-in times. Support messages contain the information you choose to send. Do not put secrets or unnecessary personal information in proposals or support messages.
LegalPages.privacyKeysBody: Your connected wallet handles private keys and signing. Epora does not ask for a seed phrase or private key. Addresses and key hashes can still identify you when linked to other information. Submitted blockchain transactions and contract data are public and can be copied worldwide. We cannot erase or change records held on the blockchain by other participants. Avoid placing names, contact details, or other private information on-chain.
LegalPages.privacyPurposesBody: We use necessary wallet and proposal data to provide the functions you request. Where data protection law requires a legal basis, providing requested functions supports performance of our agreement with you. Public blockchain indexing, service security, abuse prevention, and fault diagnosis support our legitimate interests in operating and protecting the service. The agreement basis does not apply to people who have no agreement with us. Legal obligations may require other processing. Where separate consent is required for optional processing, it must be requested separately from beta risk acceptance.
LegalPages.privacyStorageBody: The service uses a session cookie to record the network and version of your beta acknowledgement. Wallet sign-in uses a separate cookie with a seven-day validity period. Browser storage can also hold your last wallet choice, address mappings, recent recipients, display preferences, proposal drafts, and pending wallet updates. These support the application and are not advertising cookies. Your browser controls persistence, including whether it restores session cookies. Clearing storage can remove settings and drafts and require you to sign in or accept the notice again.
LegalPages.privacyDiagnosticsBody: Hosting systems receive technical connection data, such as IP addresses, request details, and browser information. Abuse controls store a hash derived from caller identity rather than a raw IP address in their database table. This is not a promise of anonymity. When Sentry error reporting is configured, it receives error details and diagnostic context. The application filters recognized sensitive fields before sending Sentry events. Other service logs may contain error details. Session replay and performance tracing are disabled in the application configuration. Error reporting, when enabled, can run before you accept the beta notice.
LegalPages.privacyRecipientsBody: Saved proposal titles, descriptions, transaction details, and signatures are visible to the creator and authorized wallet participants, including before blockchain submission. Hosting and database providers process data needed to run the service. Blockfrost and Koios process chain-data requests. Blockfrost may also receive signed transactions for submission. If you use mobile pairing, WalletConnect/Reown supplies relay services. Your chosen wallet receives connection and signing requests. Sentry receives diagnostics when configured. Public blockchain participants receive data included in submitted transactions. We may disclose data when legally required or when necessary to address fraud, security incidents, or legal claims. Contact us for details about the providers used by the hosted service.
LegalPages.privacyTransfersBody: 41BIT LLC is a United States company. Service providers and blockchain participants may process data outside your country. Provider regions and transfer arrangements depend on the hosted deployment. Where applicable data protection law restricts an international transfer, the transfer requires a valid legal mechanism. Contact us for the locations and safeguards that apply to your data. Public blockchain publication makes transaction data available worldwide.
LegalPages.privacyRetentionBody: Retention depends on the purpose of the record, operational needs, and applicable legal duties. Public blockchain records persist independently of us. Off-chain wallet indexes, proposals, signatures, and sign-in registrations do not all have automatic deletion periods. Expiry of an authentication challenge or rate-limit window does not mean its database record is immediately deleted. Provider logs and backups have separate retention settings. Contact us for current retention details or to request deletion. We may need to retain records for legal obligations or claims, and blockchain copies cannot be deleted by us.
LegalPages.privacyRightsBody: Depending on applicable law, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, or a portable copy of personal data. You may be able to object to processing based on legitimate interests. Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it without affecting earlier lawful processing. You may complain to your competent data protection authority. Send requests to the contact below. We may need proportionate identity checks, but will never ask for your seed phrase or private key. Some requests have legal exceptions or cannot change public blockchain data.
LegalPages.privacyChangesBody: We may update this policy when the service or its data practices change. The document version identifies the current text. Material changes to the beta terms or risk disclosures require a new acknowledgement. Read the current policy before supplying information or using wallet features.
LegalPages.termsReleaseBody: By selecting the separate release checkbox or sending an explicit API acknowledgement of the current terms, you release the Released Parties from all liability for losses arising from your use of this beta, to the extent permitted by applicable law. This includes loss, theft, or locking of funds and assets, and loss of data or profits. This release does not cover fraud, gross negligence, or intentional misconduct. It does not waive mandatory consumer rights or other rights that cannot lawfully be waived.
LegalPages.termsOperatorBody: 41BIT LLC is the sole service operator and contracting party. Individual members, managers, officers, employees, developers, and contributors are not parties to this agreement and give no personal guarantees by working on Epora. To the extent permitted by law, claims based solely on company obligations under these terms must be brought against 41BIT LLC, not against an individual solely because of their role in developing or operating Epora. This does not exclude liability for a person's own conduct where the law does not permit exclusion.
LegalPages.termsPartiesTitle: People and entities covered by the release
LegalPages.termsPartiesBody: The Released Parties are 41BIT LLC; its members, managers, officers, employees, affiliates, agents, and contractors; and Epora developers, maintainers, contributors, authors, and copyright holders. The release covers their involvement in developing, maintaining, distributing, or operating Epora. Including someone in this release does not make them a service operator, contracting party, or personal guarantor. Each Released Party is an intended beneficiary of the release and liability exclusions, to the extent permitted by law.
